chapter.title: The Self-Image: Your Key to Living Without Limits

concepts.title: Self-image as working self-description
concepts.content: An accumulated working picture of what kind of person one is can influence what one attempts and expects. The chapter attributes the picture to interpreted triumphs, failures, humiliation, and feedback, especially early-life experiences. The text describes the picture as a premise against which experience is judged.

concepts.author_mechanism: The chapter attributes the picture to interpreted triumphs, failures, humiliation, and feedback, especially early-life experiences. The text describes the picture as a premise against which experience is judged.
concepts.conditions_and_limits: The text claims absolute control over all actions; do not present that universal assertion as an established law.

concepts.title: Snap-back and self-confirming loops
concepts.content: Attempts to change a habit may falter when a familiar identity expectation persists. The author compares behavioral relapse with a rubber band returning to its original position and describes reinforcing cycles in which outcomes seem to prove an old identity.

concepts.thesis: Attempts to change a habit may falter when a familiar identity expectation persists.

terms.definition: Attempts to change a habit may falter when a familiar identity expectation persists.

concepts.author_mechanism: The author compares behavioral relapse with a rubber band returning to its original position and describes reinforcing cycles in which outcomes seem to prove an old identity.
concepts.conditions_and_limits: Avoid blame-laden interpretations of weight, eating or body appearance; no automatic relapse is inevitable.
concepts.application: After a setback, separate the event, strategy, interpretation and next attempt instead of inferring a permanent ceiling.
concepts.common_misreading: Treating a conceptual or anecdotal explanation as a universal causal law, without evaluating context, skills or competing explanations.
concepts.alternative_explanation: Habit cues, stress, skills, access, reinforcement and sleep can explain relapse without a self-image thermostat.
concepts.ethical_clinical_cautions: Avoid blame-laden interpretations of weight, eating or body appearance; no automatic relapse is inevitable.

concepts.title: Inside-out change versus surface affirmation
concepts.content: A positive statement about an outcome can ring hollow when it contradicts a deeply held view of the person pursuing it. The chapter contrasts treating superficial symptoms or circumstances with revisiting underlying identity judgments.

concepts.author_mechanism: The chapter contrasts treating superficial symptoms or circumstances with revisiting underlying identity judgments.
concepts.conditions_and_limits: Do not imply that affirmations are always useless or that belief change alone is sufficient.
concepts.application: Choose a credible self-description supported by at least 2 actual instances rather than demand instant confidence.

concepts.content: People may accept information congruent with their self-concept and resist information that contradicts it. Prescott Lecky is credited with a personality-wide consistency idea, illustrated by students who allegedly improved after changing self-labels.

concepts.title: Surgery, appearance and subjective identity
concepts.content: An external cosmetic change does not reliably produce a corresponding change in how someone perceives or values themself. The narrator contrasts striking post-surgery social changes with patients who retain shame and a negative self-perception despite successful procedures.

concepts.author_mechanism: The narrator contrasts striking post-surgery social changes with patients who retain shame and a negative self-perception despite successful procedures.

educational_exercises.title: Identity statement audit
educational_exercises.content: An optional PCI original activity: Record 3 frequently repeated statements starting with “I am”. For each, separate an observed event from an identity conclusion. Identify a counterexample, or say none is currently known. Create a more precise time- and task-bounded statement.

educational_exercises.timing: self-paced; choose a short comfortable session; no fixed regimen
educational_exercises.rubric: Score 0-2 each: distinguishes fact from identity; gives balanced evidence; gives non-shaming replacement; acknowledges uncertainty. Total 0-8. Self-review is not a trait score.

educational_exercises.safety: Skip if upsetting. For health, self-harm, eating-disorder or severe mental-health concerns seek appropriate professional help.

educational_exercises.title: One identity-consistent action
educational_exercises.content: An optional PCI original activity: Choose one modest action avoided because of a negative identity label. Write a measurable prediction and a practical obstacle. Attempt the action with consent and support where needed. Compare prediction and outcome; record one non-identity explanation.

claims.title: Book claim: Self-image as working self-description
claims.content: An accumulated working picture of what kind of person one is can influence what one attempts and expects. The chapter explains it as follows: The chapter attributes the picture to interpreted triumphs, failures, humiliation, and feedback, especially early-life experiences. The text describes the picture as a premise against which experience is judged.

claims.title: Book claim: Snap-back and self-confirming loops
claims.content: Attempts to change a habit may falter when a familiar identity expectation persists.
